weeks.label: Week 1
weeks.goal: Establish daily habits, activate the right muscles, and introduce gentle movement without pain.

principles.title: Glute engagement
principles.text: Keep glutes gently active all day.

weeks.notes:
DAILY BASICS - DO THESE EVERY DAY (ALL 6 WEEKS)

THIS IS WEEK 1
Keep everything pain-free and controlled. RANGE IS SMALL. EFFORT IS LOW. CONSISTENCY IS KEY.

PROGRESSION PREVIEW:
Over the next 5 weeks we will gradually increase: range of motion, weight, effort, and control to rebuild strong, pain-free knees.
weeks.editorNotes: Header: "WEEK 1: FOUNDATION". Key principles row titled "KEY PRINCIPLES FOR WEEK 1". Cards 1-2 sit under the banner "DAILY BASICS - DO THESE EVERY DAY (ALL 6 WEEKS)" (banner text kept in notes). Label removed: "Bottom panel:".

exercises.name: Roll Out Quads – Daily
howTo: Use a foam roller or rolling pin.
Roll slowly over the entire front of your thigh (quad).
Focus on tight or tender areas.
exercises.why: Helps rule out telefemoral pain syndrome (tight quads causing knee pain) and improves tissue quality.

exercises.name: Basic Glute Engagement – All Day
howTo: Gently engage your glutes as if you are "squeezing a credit card" between your cheeks.
exercises.why: Tight quads often cause knee pain. Glute activation helps take pressure off the knee.
focus: Engage gently (about 10-20% effort) throughout your day.
exercises.whyItMatters: Strong, active glutes reduce quad dominance and help protect your knees.

exercises.name: Knee Circles (Low Range) – Daily
howTo: Stand tall holding onto a wall or support if needed.
Put as little weight as your knee can tolerate WITHOUT pain.
Do NOT move hip or ankle.
exercises.directions: Perform slow, controlled circles in each direction.

other.Focus: Control and comfort NOT depth or speed

exercises.name: Isometric Hamstring Wall Heel Dig – Daily
howTo: Lie on your back with heel against the wall.
Dig heel gently into the wall.

dosage.hold: Hold for 5-10 seconds at about 40-50% effort.

exercises.name: Quadriceps Squeeze (Full Lockout) – Daily
howTo: Lit or lie with leg straight.
Tighten your quad and push knee down into the floor (or pad/towel).

dosage.hold: Hold for 5-10 seconds at about 40-50% effort.

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.goal: Gradually increase load and strength while maintaining excellent control and pain-free movement.

exercises.name: Knee Traction – 3 to 10 Times Per Day
howTo: Place a rolled towel behind your knee.
Use a light pole or PVC pipe across your thigh just above the knee.
Gently pull upward to create traction.

exercises.name: Knee Circles (Low Range) – Daily
howTo: Stand tall holding onto a wall or support.
Put as much weight as your knee can tolerate WITHOUT pain.
Do NOT move hip or ankle.
exercises.whatsNew: Increase the weight slightly from Week 1 if pain-free. Circle size can be a little bigger than Week 1, but still keep it small and controlled.

other.Focus: Control and comfort NOT depth or speed

howTo: Sit or lie with leg fully straight.
Tighten quad and push knee down.
exercises.whatsNew: Increase effort to about 50-60% of your maximum strength.

weeks.label: Week 3
weeks.goal: Increase knee circle range, reduce load if needed, and add backward walking to build control and strength.

principles.title: Glute engagement

DAILY BASICS - DO THESE EVERY DAY

THIS IS WEEK 3
We continue to build CONTROL and RANGE OF MOTION. Reduce weight if needed. Increase circle size only if pain-free. Backward walking adds strength without joint compression.

PROGRESSION PREVIEW:
Weeks 4-6 will continue to increase:
- Range of motion for knee circles
- Strength of quad contractions
- Distance of backward walking
- Overall control and stability

REMEMBER:
Consistency beats intensity. Small, daily wins lead to stronger, pain-free knees.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat (Assisted to Start) – Daily
howTo: Shift your weight to one side while keeping the other leg straight.
Keep heel down on the bent leg.
Keep knee wide in line with toes.
Use support (TRX, pole, counter, or bench) as needed.

other.Focus: Heel down, knee wide, hips back, full control.

exercises.proTip: Start with partial range and support. As mobility and strength improve, go deeper and reduce the amount of support.

exercises.name: Optional Add-Ons (If Tolerated)
exercises.whenToUse: Add these if they do not increase knee pain or irritation.
howTo: HIP FLEXOR STRETCH: 2-3 sets, 30-45 sec each
focus: Improve overall mobility, balance and recovery.

exercises.name: Continue Daily Maintenance
exercises.whatsNew: This week is about mastering full range of motion, deep knee control, and functional strength. Keep knee circles in your routine long-term to maintain healthy, pain-free knees.
exercises.inPerpetuity: Knee circles are a lifetime maintenance tool. Keep them in your routine!
